gaps: The local artifact inspector requires no Azure, Graph or Defender permissions and performs no authentication or service queries. Its target and receipt hashes are caller-selected local evidence, not approved grants or effective authorization. Source: scripts/Sysmon.ArtifactValidation.psm1 SHA256 369043d8535f28badb045c701fdb336124ec3f733852ce616d44a507a035d041; scripts/Test-DeploymentArtifacts.ps1 SHA256 7ae735125b9819926b7063d95740b15cc18e12a5add4e0a7ccee6be7857c44b0.

Azure deployment, DCR/VM association and cleanup roles have not been exhaustively mapped in this assessment. Existing scripts and target-specific authorization remain authoritative; no additional roles are granted.

Defender Live Response publishing and cleanup refer to Library.Manage, but effective operator roles, licensing and endpoint execution permissions remain unverified. Library publication is not execution or delivery.

Existing Intune cleanup, group access, all other optional paths and tenant-wide AMA association requirements are not completely represented. Partial coverage must not be used to consent or grant permissions.

Optional service-api-smoke uses only GET but Defender library listing still requires broad Library.Manage (delegated or application); this source is not approval to grant it. Existing target-scope Microsoft.Insights/monitoredObjects/read and subscription provider-metadata read, service licensing, administrator roles, OIDC/FIC prerequisites and effective access remain operator-verified gaps; the scheduled workflow starts disabled and provisions none of them.
